notes: "This is where it started. In group meetings I see more and more slides made with AI, and I think that is the direction things are going: slides are data, a file format, so of course agents will learn to make them. But my advisor, and most people in the room, can tell at a glance when a deck was made by AI. Each tool has its own style, PowerPoint, Google Slides, ChatGPT, Kimi, and they all still look like AI. I read a post on Xiaohongshu that put it well: the AI look comes from having no focus, from covering everything, from having no story, from aiming to be complete and safe. Even this talk fell into it. On the right are pages from the previous version, made by Claude Code. They look fine. My comment on them was: the visuals are good, but there is no focus, because there is no story. That is the problem this project is about."

designIntent.purpose: Reason 1: AI-made slides are recognisable at a glance; the AI look comes from no focus and no story.
keep: Previous-version thumbnails are real renders of this project
Owner quote attributed and marked as translated
Personal observation, not a research finding
